# Moment

A moment in an app's life, shown in the space it is given: nothing here yet, on its way, something failed, a first run, or something finished. It holds art (any node, usually an inline SVG), a title, one line and up to two actions. It renders in the page's flow and never floats over what the person is using; its celebration stays inside the art's frame.

```tsx
import { Moment } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/moment/moment";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Moment
  art={<EmptyInbox />}
  title="No messages yet"
  description="Messages you send show up here."
  action={<Button onClick={compose}>New message</Button>}
/>
<Moment kind="success" art={<Done />} title="All caught up" dismissKey="caught-up" cap={{ times: 1, per: "day" }} />
```

## Usage

Moments behave so they never get in the way: the art is decorative unless labelled, the art's own motion stops with reduced motion, the close button keeps a dismissal through `dismissKey`, `cap` limits how often a success celebrates, and `quiet` (or `MomentProvider`) makes them compact. The root carries `data-moment` (the kind), `data-celebrate` while it celebrates and `data-quiet` when quiet.

## Use instead when

- Use `Empty` instead for a plain empty list with an icon and no art, `Alert` for a message about something that happened beside the content, `Skeleton` for the shape of content that is loading, and `toast()` to confirm an everyday action.

## Props

Type: `MomentProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | The way forward, usually one `Button`: `action={<Button onClick={compose}>New message</Button>}`. |
| `announce` | `boolean` |  | Speaks a `success` or `error` moment politely to screen readers when it appears: the title, then the description when it is text. Other kinds are never spoken. |
| `art` | `ReactNode` |  | The picture: any node, usually an inline SVG, which fills the art's height (160px, 96px when the moment is narrower than 24rem, 40px when quiet, 24px inline). It is decorative and hidden from screen readers unless you pass `artLabel`. Draw it with `currentColor` and the theme's variables so it follows the kind, the theme and dark mode. With reduced motion, its CSS animations stop and its SVG animations pause. |
| `artLabel` | `string` |  | Names the art for screen readers (`role="img"`), for a picture that says something the title does not. |
| `cap` | `{ times: number; per: "day" \| "week" \| "month" \| "ever" \| (string & { 'Use "day", "week", "month" or "ever"': never }) }` |  | Shows the flourish at most `times` times `per` day, week, 30-day month or ever, counted in `localStorage` under the moment's `dismissKey`, or its `id`; after that the moment is quiet. Without a key the flourish shows every time the moment appears. |
| `celebrate` | `boolean` | `true` for `kind="success"`, otherwise `false` | A short flourish when the moment appears: a soft disc swells from behind the art and four sparks grow and fade, all inside the art's frame. With reduced motion only the disc fades. Never when quiet or inline. Capped with `cap`. |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mt-6`). Appearance classes warn in development; use `kind` and `quiet`. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | One line on what to do or what it means: "Messages you send show up here." |
| `dismissKey` | `string` |  | Keeps a dismissal: once the person closes the moment, it stays closed on every visit and in every tab, stored in `localStorage` as `ouro-moment:dismissed:<dismissKey>`. Shows the close button. With it the moment renders nothing until the browser has said whether it was dismissed, so a server-rendered page never flashes a closed moment. |
| `dismissLabel` | `string` | `"Dismiss"` | The close button's accessible name, for other languages. |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6` | `3`, and no heading with `size="inline"` | The title's heading level. Pick the level below the section the moment sits in. Inline, the title is plain text unless you pass one. |
| `kind` | `"loading" \| "success" \| "error" \| "empty" \| "welcome"` | `"empty"` | What the moment is about. `empty`: nothing here yet. `loading`: on its way, with a spinner when there is no art. `error`: something failed. `welcome`: a first run. `success`: something finished, which celebrates (see `celebrate`). The kind colours the art's `currentColor` from the theme and is on the root as `data-moment`. |
| `onDismiss` | `(() => void)` |  | Shows a quiet close button. Pressing it hides the moment, hands focus to what follows it, and calls this. |
| `quiet` | `boolean` | the nearest `MomentProvider`'s `quiet`, or `false` | A compact row: 40px art, the title and one line, no celebration. For dense panes, and for people who want less: set it for the whole app with `MomentProvider`. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `secondaryAction` | `ReactNode` |  | A second, quieter way, beside `action`: `secondaryAction={<Button variant="plain">Learn more</Button>}`. Two at most. |
| `size` | `"inline" \| "default"` | `"default"` | `default` stacks the art, title, line and actions in the space it is given. `inline` is a single row with 24px art, for a "working" row in a list or toolbar. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | What happened or what is here, in a few words: "Inbox cleared". Required, because it is what a screen reader finds. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `actions`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `action` and `secondaryAction`: `<Moment action={<Button>Retry</Button>}>`.
- `body`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `description`: `<Moment description="Messages you send show up here.">`.
- `heading`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `title`: `<Moment title="No messages yet">`.
- `icon`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `art`: `<Moment art={<Illustration />}>`.
- `illustration`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `art`: `<Moment art={<Illustration />}>`.
- `onClose`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `onDismiss`: `<Moment onDismiss={() => setOpen(false)}>`.
- `variant`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `kind`: `<Moment kind="error">`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: Moment merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
